topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Arrows to Spaces

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Arrows to Spaces

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Magnitude & Direction)
sections.content: Define a vector as a directed line segment. Introduce the concept of a coordinate system where a vector is an arrow starting from the origin (0,0) to a point (x,y).
sections.example: A GPS coordinate tracking a bird flying from its nest at (0,0) to a tree at (3,2).

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule
sections.content: Explain how to add two vectors visually. Place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first. The result is the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors.
sections.example: A boat moving across a river: Vector A is the boat's speed, Vector B is the river's current. The resulting movement is Vector A + Vector B.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Arrow
sections.content: Introduce multiplying a vector by a scalar (a real number). Explain that it changes the vector's length (scaling) and can reverse its direction if the scalar is negative.
sections.example: A superhero 'scaling' their jump: If Vector V is a 2-meter jump, 3V is a 6-meter leap, and -1V is jumping backwards.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Basis Vectors
sections.content: Explain how any 2D vector can be formed by combining the unit vectors 'i' (1,0) and 'j' (0,1). This introduces the concept of the 'span' of a vector space.
sections.example: A 2D game character moving on a grid: Any movement can be broken down into 'x' horizontal steps and 'y' vertical steps.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Linear Transformations
sections.content: Briefly summarize how these basic operations allow us to move, rotate, and resize entire spaces, forming the foundation of computer graphics and AI.
sections.example: The 'pinch-to-zoom' gesture on a smartphone screen, which is mathematically just a matrix transformation applied to a grid of vectors.

storyboard.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Magnitude & Direction)
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.
Visualize them starting from the origin.
A bird flies from nest at origin.
animations: # Animation 1 (Hook): Dot appears at origin, then grows into a vector arrow toward (3,2). Color: #FFD700 (Gold) for arrow. Label "(0,0)" at start, "(3,2)" at head.
# Animation 2 (Prerequisites): Draw grid lines lightly in #404040. Highlight (3,2) coordinate.
# Animation 3 (Definition): Label the vector as 'v'. Show the distance formula as sqrt(3^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(13). Color: #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue) for formula.
# Animation 4 (Demonstration): Move the vector tail to (1,1) and point to (4,3). Show that the arrow shape is identical.
# Animation 5 (Application): Animate the vector as a 'path' of a bird from (0,0) to (3,2). Label path 'Bird Path'. Color: #32CD32 (Lime Green).

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule
lecture_lines: Place the second tail at the first head.
Form a parallelogram with these two vectors.
The diagonal is the sum of vectors.
Like a boat moving across a current.
animations: # Animation 1: Show Vector A (blue) and Vector B (red). Place them starting at origin. Color A: #00BFFF, Color B: #FF4500.
# Animation 2: Shift Vector B so its tail starts at the head of A. Highlight the parallelogram formed by A and B. Color: #FFFFFF (White) for dotted outline.
# Animation 3: Draw the resultant vector (sum) from origin to the far vertex of the parallelogram. Label as 'A + B'. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).

storyboard.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Arrow
lecture_lines: Scaling stretches or shrinks a vector.
Multiplying by 3 triples the arrow length.
Negative scalars reverse the vector direction.
animations: # Animation 1: Show Vector V. Color: #00BFFF. Stretch V to 3V (longer arrow) and 0.5V (shorter arrow). Label each clearly.
# Animation 2: Show V then animate it rotating 180 degrees to show -V. Color: #FF4500 (Red). Highlight the reversal.
# Animation 3: Display a number line (scalar) next to the vector. As the scalar slider moves from -2 to 2, the vector scales and flips in real-time.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations and Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Basis vectors 'i' and 'j' define the space.
Any 2D vector is a combination of them.
This grid movement is a linear combination.
animations: # Animation 1: Show unit vectors i=(1,0) in #FFD700 and j=(0,1) in #32CD32. Grid background on.
# Animation 2: Represent a vector v=(3,2) as 3*i + 2*j. Show it visually as three 'i' arrows and two 'j' arrows stacking up.
# Animation 3: Fade out the grid lines. Show that any point (x,y) can be reached by a combination of i and j. Label 'Span'. Color: #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Power of Linear Transformations
lecture_lines: Transformations move, rotate, and resize spaces.
These operations form the basis of AI.
Like pinching to zoom on your screen.
animations: # Animation 1: Show a 2D grid of dots. Animate the grid shifting and rotating. Label 'Transformation'. Color: #00BFFF.
# Animation 2: Simulate a 'pinch-to-zoom' on the grid. Vectors on the grid grow/shrink relative to the center. Color: #FFD700.
# Animation 3: Reveal a 2x2 matrix display changing as the grid changes. Highlight connection between matrix and vector movement. Color: #32CD32.
